hero.title: One class, many objects
intro.0: You have written a class and made an object from it. So how many objects can one class make?
intro.1: It is easy to read a class as if it were the thing itself - one Cat class, one cat. That reading holds up until the day you need a second cat, and then everything you hardcoded inside the class turns out to be shared by every cat you make.
intro.2: Here you write the code and watch memory while it runs. Each new puts another object on screen, side by side, each with its own values - which is the difference between the blueprint and the things built from it.
task.1.title: A second cat
task.1.context:
One class can make as many objects as you ask for. Each `new Cat(...)` sets aside its own slot in memory, so two cats are two separate things - not two names for one thing.

The code below makes one cat called Ana. Make a second cat with a different name, and describe it too. Then press Visualize and watch memory: you are looking for two cards, not one.
task.1.goal.0: Two `Cat` objects exist at the same time.
task.1.goal.1: The two cats hold different names.
task.2.title: Same name, different cat
task.2.context:
Two objects can hold the same name and still be two different cats. What makes them separate is not what they are called - it is that each one got its own slot when `new` ran.

Make a second cat also called Ana, but a different age. Visualize it and read the two cards: the same name twice, two ages, two objects.
task.2.goal.0: Two `Cat` objects exist at the same time.
task.2.goal.1: The two cats hold different ages.
task.3.title: Three at once
task.3.context:
There is no limit written anywhere. A class is a shape; you can stamp out as many objects from it as the program needs, and each one is another card in memory.

Make three cats, each with its own name, and describe all three. Visualize it: three cards, three names, one class.
task.3.goal.0: Three `Cat` objects exist at the same time.
task.4.summaryIntro: A class is the shape; each `new` makes another object with that shape and its own values. You did not take that on trust - the cards you watched appear came from your own code actually running.
task.4.summaryItems.0.title: Class -
task.4.summaryItems.0.text: the blueprint. Written once, it says what every object made from it will hold.
task.4.summaryItems.1.title: Instance -
task.4.summaryItems.1.text: one object made from that class. `new Cat()` makes one; three `new Cat()` calls make three.
task.4.summaryItems.2.title: Its own values -
task.4.summaryItems.2.text: each instance holds its own `Name` and `Age`. Writing to one leaves the others alone.
task.4.summaryClose: Next you will stop setting those values line by line after the object exists, and pass them in at the moment it is made.
concept.pr-instance.def: One object made from a class. Several instances of one class each hold their own values.
